headline: Committee discusses Bill 76 water fee change and an overnight parking ban

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: The committee discussed Bill 76, which would base the water system development fee on daily water use rather than meter size, and took testimony on a parking ban. The chair said the parking bill will return with Public Works, police and Human Concerns present.
meeting.recap: The committee discussed Bill 76, which would base the water system development fee on daily water use, not meter size.[[0:04:01]] Staff said one equivalent single dwelling, a standard unit, equals 300 gallons a day.[[0:12:20]] Staff said properties already legally connected would not pay the fee again.[[0:15:08]] Affordable and workforce housing projects could pay the fee later, when the impact happens.[[0:15:42]] A testifier said it was unclear how the new fee would be applied.[[0:19:43]] Staff said fees for a small single-family meter would be very similar to before.[[0:38:47]] The councilmember presenting it said police could not enforce the existing overnight ban.[[1:07:58]] One testifier asked the committee to pause the bill.[[1:11:09]] A second testifier strongly opposed it.[[1:17:35]] A councilmember said the Department of Human Concerns will update the council on safe parking on June 29th.[[1:30:00]] The chair said the bill will return with Public Works, police and Human Concerns present.[[1:41:04]]
meeting.next: A councilmember said they will work on updating the Lahaina section of the parking code so it is consistent.

issues.oneLine: Bill 76 would change the water system development fee to be based on average daily demand instead of meter size.
issues.why: The chair said the change makes the fee more accurately reflect a project's actual impact on the county's water source and storage.

deadlines.t: Second and final reading of Bill 76 at the Council.

issues.next: Bill 76 is scheduled for second and final reading on June 5th, 2026.
issues.brief: One equivalent single dwelling is a standard unit equal to 300 gallons of water a day.[[#1]] Staff said the fee had not been raised in quite some time and was well overdue for this restructuring.[[#2]] Staff said future budgets plan a 2 to 3 percent yearly increase in the fee.[[#3]]

issues.oneLine: A testifier said many people live in their vehicles and the county has never established safe parking.
issues.why: A testifier said the parking ban would make life more dangerous for working families, kūpuna and disaster survivors struggling in Maui's housing crisis.

deadlines.t: Department of Human Concerns update on safe parking.

issues.next: The Department of Human Concerns is set to give the council an update on safe parking on June 29th.
issues.brief: A testifier asked the county to set up safe overnight parking with sanitation and security.[[#1]] A councilmember cited a news report that the unsheltered population rose by about 40 percent.[[#2]] The bill's presenter said there was no clear answer on when the safe parking program will start.[[#3]]
